title: Cult has three acts: intellect of excellence, will’s inward bow, and outward signs of subjection
source_text: I. Ante omnia Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, ac Bellarminus in primis, observant cultum in genere tres diversos actus complecti. Et primo actum intellectus quo apprehendimus ejus quem colimus excellentiam. Secundo actum voluntatis, quo nos illi interius inclinamus, & aliquid volumus facere actu interiore, vel exteriore, quo protestemur ejus excellentiam, & nostram subjectionem. Tertio actum exteriorem, quo caput inclinamus, vel genu flectimus, vel aliquod aliud signum subjectionis ostendimus. De Sanctorum Beatitudine lib. 1. cap. 12.
pass_a_gloss: Before all things the Doctors of the Roman Church, and Bellarmine especially, observe that cult in general embraces three diverse acts. And first the act of the intellect by which we apprehend the excellence of him whom we cultivate. Second the act of the will, by which we incline ourselves inwardly to him, and we will to do something by an interior or exterior act, by which we protest his excellence and our subjection. Third the exterior act, by which we incline the head, or bend the knee, or show some other sign of subjection. On the Beatitude of the Saints, book 1, chapter 12.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors (Bellarmino first) say cult wraps three acts.
Intellect grasps the excellence; will bows inward and wills a protest of that excellence and our subjection.
Outward signs follow—head bowed, knee bent, or the like.

choices.why: Scholastic sense of outwardly attesting excellence.
